question: At what age range do girls typically experience their pubertal growth spurt?
explanation: Girls typically experience their pubertal growth spurt earlier than boys, usually around 10 to 12 years of age. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why are nutritional requirements proportionally very high during the adolescent growth spurt?

options.B: Rapid skeletal, muscular, and hormonal changes increase metabolic demands
options.C: Adolescents stop growing completely after age 10
options.D: Nutritional needs are actually lower than in infancy

explanation: The rapid skeletal, muscular, and hormonal changes during puberty significantly increase the body's demand for energy and nutrients. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why is adequate protein intake especially crucial during the adolescent growth spurt?

options.B: To support the expansion of lean body mass and muscle development

explanation: Protein provides the essential building blocks needed to support the rapid expansion of lean body mass, organs, and skeletal muscle during puberty. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h2)

question: Which two micronutrients are primarily responsible for maximizing peak bone mass during adolescence?
explanation: Calcium and Vitamin D work closely together to ensure proper bone mineralization and maximize peak bone mass during the adolescent years. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary tool used to evaluate BMI status in growing adolescents?
explanation: Because adolescents are still growing, their BMI must be plotted against age- and sex-specific growth charts to accurately assess their weight status. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h3)

question: Which anthropometric measurement is commonly used in resource-constrained settings for a quick screen of acute malnutrition?
explanation: Mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) is a quick, practical screening tool used to assess acute nutritional status in various healthcare settings. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why are adolescent girls particularly vulnerable to iron-deficiency anemia?

options.A: They consume too much vitamin C
options.B: The onset of menstruation combined with inadequate dietary iron intake
options.C: They have slower metabolism rates than boys
options.D: Excessive intake of dairy products blocks iron

explanation: Menstrual blood loss combined with diets low in bioavailable iron puts adolescent girls at a significantly higher risk for iron-deficiency anemia. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which dietary combination can a nurse recommend to improve the absorption of non-heme iron from plant sources?

options.A: Iron sources combined with calcium-rich milk
options.B: Iron sources combined with vitamin C-rich foods
options.C: Iron sources combined with high-sodium foods
options.D: Iron sources eaten alone on an empty stomach

explanation: Consuming vitamin C along with plant-based (non-heme) iron significantly enhances the body's ability to absorb the iron. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which eating disorder is primarily characterized by severe caloric restriction and an intense fear of gaining weight?
explanation: Anorexia nervosa involves self-starvation, severe caloric restriction, and an intense fear of weight gain driven by a distorted body image. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is a common physical or behavioral warning sign associated with bulimia nervosa?

options.B: Binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors like purging
options.C: Complete lack of interest in food or calories
options.D: Increased bone density and height velocity

explanation: Bulimia nervosa is marked by cycles of binge eating followed by purging or other compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h5)

question: What lifestyle factor has significantly contributed to the rise of adolescent obesity?

options.A: High consumption of leafy green vegetables
options.B: Shift toward energy-dense processed foods and sedentary screen time
options.D: Strict adherence to traditional low-calorie Nigerian staples

explanation: The shift toward processed, energy-dense foods combined with sedentary habits like screen time is a major driver of adolescent obesity. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h6)

question: Which chronic health condition is increasingly diagnosed in adolescents due to rising rates of obesity?
explanation: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, once considered an adult disease, is now increasingly diagnosed in adolescents due to rising obesity and metabolic risk. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why does adolescent pregnancy carry a uniquely high nutritional risk?

options.A: Teenagers have lower nutrient needs than adult women
options.B: The adolescent is still growing herself while also nourishing a fetus
options.C: Fetal growth stops completely during teenage pregnancies
options.D: Pregnant teens are completely immune to anemia

explanation: Competing demands occur because the adolescent body needs nutrients for its own growth alongside the requirements of the developing fetus. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h7)

question: What are common infant complications associated with inadequate nutrition in pregnant adolescents?

options.B: Low birth weight and preterm birth

explanation: Inadequate nutrition in pregnant teens often leads to intrauterine growth restriction, resulting in low birth weight and preterm birth. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h7)

question: What counseling technique can nurses use to help adolescents explore ambivalence and set personal dietary goals?
explanation: Motivational interviewing is an empathetic, patient-centered counseling technique that helps individuals explore ambivalence and build intrinsic motivation for change. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h8)

question: In addition to individual counseling, what is an important nursing responsibility in community health regarding adolescent nutrition?

options.A: Prescribing surgical interventions for all teens
options.B: Assessing household food security and collaborating with interprofessional teams
options.C: Restricting all dietary education to hospital wards
options.D: Encouraging complete elimination of local food staples

explanation: Nurses must assess household food security and work alongside dietitians and social workers to provide comprehensive nutritional care. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h8)
